name: Andorra

income_tax.summary: IRPF is a flat 10% on the general base after a EUR 24,000 personal minimum, minus a bonus of 50% of the tax on that base capped at EUR 800, so the effective marginal rates are 0% to EUR 24,000, 5% from EUR 24,000 to 40,000 and 10% above. Employees pay 6.5% CASS (pensions 3.5% + general 3%); the self-employed 22% of a chosen base, ceiling EUR 3,674.72 a month.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: CASS self-employed: 22% (10% general branch + 12% pensions) of a chosen base set as a share of the previous year's mean monthly salary: 25% (EUR 668.13, EUR 146.99/month, restricted to certain criteria), 50% (EUR 1,568.67), 75% (EUR 2,004.39), 100% (EUR 2,672.52, EUR 587.95/month, the DEFAULT for those who do not qualify for a reduced rate), 125% (EUR 3,340.65) and 137.5% (EUR 3,674.72, EUR 808.44/month, requires higher net income or turnover). The recorded 22% with a cap of 12 x EUR 3,674.72 = EUR 44,096.64 reproduces the TOP tier (EUR 9,701 a year, about 18% of EUR 54k); the default 100% tier would be EUR 7,055 a year, about 13% of EUR 54k. Figures are from the CASS page updated 30 January 2025; 2026 amounts were not found and the CASS site says it is informational only.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No municipal income tax. The 0% and 5% bands model the EUR 24,000 personal minimum and the EUR 800 bonus; the guide is for tax year 2025, the 2026 guide was not opened. Residents with more than 183 days or the centre of economic interests in Andorra are taxed on worldwide income.

Deductions available to employees (e.g. CASS contributions) were not extracted; the guide shows them as images.

regimes.name: Residence for digital nomads (D.3)
regimes.description: Residence authorisation (D.3) for any newcomer, EU or non-EU, whose work requires no fixed geographic location and uses telecommunications and technology (Govern d'Andorra). Conditions: a favourable ruling from the ministry in charge of the economy that the applicant's work is location-independent, admission within the regulatory quota, effective principal residence in Andorra for at least 90 days a calendar year, proof of owned or rented housing meeting minimum standards (or purchase under way), sufficient financial means as set by regulation, and health and disability insurance valid in Andorra. Initial authorisation two years, first renewal two years, second renewal three years, later renewals ten years. The visa itself does not change tax: residents (183 days or centre of economic interests) pay IRPF on worldwide income under the standard schedule. The income threshold and quota are set by regulation and were not found.
regimes.duration_note: 2 + 2 + 3 years, then 10-year renewals (Govern d'Andorra); 7 years counted as the first three periods.

residence_routes: Andorra is outside the EU; EU, US and other citizens all need a residence authorisation. The Govern d'Andorra lists, among others: residence without work (passive; investment amounts and the financial-authority deposit not verified here), residence and work for employees (quota-based) and for the self-employed (J.1/J.2, including foreign-investment reservations), residence for entrepreneur programme participants (D.4), and a digital nomad residence (D.3: quota, location-independent work cleared by the economy ministry, at least 90 days a year in Andorra, initial two years then 2, 3 and 10-year renewals). Amounts and quotas were not verified.
open_questions: Residence-permit amounts and quotas (passive residence, work, nomad) were not found: the Govern pages list conditions but defer figures to regulations.
No expat tax regime was found; not positively ruled out from an official source.
Rents rest on one aggregator (Global Property Guide); a relocation consultancy quoted EUR 1,300 to 1,600 for a 2-bedroom in June 2026 (not used); no second source opened.
